slides.heading: Calling Functions
slides.body: Calling Functions is part of Functions and Modularity. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Calling Functions
slides.body: Calling a function means running it by writing its name followed by parentheses. A function does nothing until it is called.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Calling a function is like pressing the start button after setting up a machine.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: A good function should do one clear task and have a name that explains that task.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Call a function named greet after defining it.
slides.hint: Write greet() after the function definition.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Define a function named alarm that prints Wake up, then call it twice.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
